nodes.description: Address of the implementation contract stored in storage slot 0 and used as the delegatecall target of the fallback function.
Constructor that permanently sets the implementation address; the implementation cannot be upgraded afterwards.
Constructor argument supplying the address of the fixed implementation contract.
External payable fallback that copies the raw calldata and delegatecalls the implementation, reverting or returning the raw returndata.
External payable receive hook that emits the Received event with msg.value, msg.sender and msg.data.
Inline-assembly delegatecall(gas(), target, ...) that executes the implementation code in the proxy storage context using caller-controlled calldata.
Caller-controlled address forwarded into the Received event emitted by the receive function.
Assembly local variable holding the implementation address loaded via sload(0) and passed to delegatecall.
Assembly local variable holding the delegatecall success flag that decides between revert and return.

edges.reason: The constructor parameter _implementation is written into the implementation state variable.
The constructor assigns _implementation to the implementation state variable in storage slot 0.
The fallback reads the implementation state variable through assembly sload(0) to build the delegatecall target.
The fallback unconditionally forwards execution into delegatecall with the caller-supplied calldata, allowing arbitrary reentrant calls into the proxy and implementation.
The assembly local target (implementation read from storage) is the destination address supplied to the delegatecall.
The success flag of the delegatecall is captured in the assembly local result, which controls revert versus raw return.
The untrusted caller address msg.sender is emitted in the Received event by the receive function.

normalization_plan.reason: The constructor parameter _implementation only carries the value written to the implementation state variable, so it is merged into the constructor function.
The assembly local target is a temporary alias of the implementation address consumed directly by the delegatecall unsafe operation.
The assembly local result is produced solely by the delegatecall and only determines whether the proxy reverts, so it is merged into the delegatecall operation.
